title: Rapid synth: KV + adaptive batching field digest
body:
Stream-of-thought synopsis and quick action list after reading a few KV/batching papers + trying a micro-probe on a small fleet. Mostly raw, intentionally choppy.

Top-level hypothesis: For our long-tail conversational workloads, combining coarse-grained KV sharding with adaptive per-request micro-batching gives the best latency/cost frontier if we can keep tail variance bounded. But tradeoffs are subtle: eviction policy + shard placement dominate at >1M tokens/hr.

What I read (fast notes):
- paper A (arXiv 2306.08609): shows per-shard hot-spotting when content popularity skew > 8x; recommends small LRU windows + periodic compaction.
- blog post on batching heuristics: greedy vs. earliest-deadline-first batchers; EDF reduces p99 at expense of throughput under high qps bursts.
- internal PR (#42): KV-shard placement prototype; naive hashing +/- ring-rebalance approach works but causes large KV transfer during resizes.

Experiment snapshot (local cluster x3 gpus):
- workload: multi-turn dialog traces sampled from beta users (median turn length ~ 70 tokens, but 5% > 1200)
- baseline: global KV (no sharding), fixed batcher (max batch=8, max latency=40ms)
- variant 1: 4-way shard, LRU-ttl 10m, batcher EDF micro-batches up to 12 tokens per micro-batch
- metrics: median latency, p95/p99, token throughput, GPU utilization, extra network xfer

Quick results (very noisy):
- baseline median 32ms, p99 210ms, gpu-util 42%
- variant 1 median 36ms, p99 120ms, gpu-util 58% (better tail, higher util)
- network tx increased ~18% due to more KV misses pulling from other shard owners

Interpretation / takeaways:
- sharding + EDF-like micro-batching reduces tail latencies by increasing utilization and allowing more compact kernel workloads, but KVMiss network costs matter for cross-shard hot items.
- a small TTL and aggressive local caching for top-k keys (hotset) reduced network tx but increased memory pressure; sweet spot looked like hotset size ~2-4% of overall keys for these traces.
- autoscale/resizing needs to prioritize minimal shard transfers: consider sticky shard-to-host with overflow buckets rather than rehash-on-resize.

Open questions / next probes:
- how does quantized KV storage affect fetch latency and memory tradeoffs? cheap wins?
- can we detect hot-key skew online and create ephemeral tiny replicas for hot items (eventual consistency ok)?
- what's the SLA impact if we degrade to global model fallback vs. best-effort shard routing? (simulate with synthetic spike tests)

Immediate TODOs (for next 2 sprints):
- run 24h compaction + shard-stability test on staging (JIRA-INF-892)
- add EDF vs. greedy batcher A/B in the loadgen harness (low-risk) — aim to measure p95/p99 with 1M+ synthetic reqs
- prototype hotset ephemeral replica: minimal coherence rules (only promote, never demote automatically) — measure memory pressure

Notes-to-self:
- talk to Lina about memory allocator knobs (we saw fragmentation on cuda pinned buffers).
- ping infra for a quieter window to run long-run stable tests.
- re-check PR #42 for TODOs re: graceful ring rebalancing (there was a comment about chunked transfers).

Rough mental model summary (one-liner): shard to raise GPU utilization and smooth kernel performance; micro-batching policy to control tail; carefully engineer cache + replication to reduce cross-shard fetch cost.

References / quick links: 
- arXiv paper above (key equations about skew and miss-rate).
- internal PR and Jira listed in linked_artifacts.

End of dump — clean up and formalize into a tech brief after running the full A/B.
